user.title: HVAC Schedule Optimizer
user.description: Pick the thermostat to schedule. If your indoor temperature comes from a separate sensor you trust more than the thermostat's own reading, add it too. Turn off any other scheduler (such as Climate Scheduler) for this thermostat so they do not fight.

abort.already_configured: This thermostat is already set up.

init.title: Comfort limits and schedule
init.description: Temperatures use your Home Assistant unit. The optimizer only proposes schedules that keep the house under these limits while cooling (heating limits are on a later page). The baseline is your current schedule, used for the savings comparison and as the starting schedule.

data.history_days: Days of history to learn from

data_description.room_sensors: Any number of indoor sensors. Each room learns how it runs compared with the thermostat (about 3 days of readings), then you choose when it counts against the comfort limits on the next page.
data_description.outdoor_sensors: Any number of outdoor sensors. Their median replaces Open-Meteo's past weather when learning, and corrects the forecast for your spot. One sensor in direct sun is outvoted when you have three or more.

rooms.title: When each room counts
rooms.description:
Choose when each room's temperature has to stay under the comfort limits: always, only during awake hours, only during sleep hours, or never (shown on the card only). The thermostat itself always counts.

{names}

presence.title: Presence
presence.description:
Pick everyone who lives here (their person entities). While all of them are out, the house is allowed to drift to the away limits, and it is back inside your comfort limits when the first person is expected home. Routines are learned per person from the last four weeks. Anyone home, or a tracker that is unavailable, means home. Leave empty to turn presence off.

The setback runs only while Run schedule is on and the model is trusted. The Guest mode switch turns it off while someone without a tracker is home.

person.title: {name}
person.description: Optional, both used only while everyone is out. A travel time sensor (Waze Travel Time, Google Travel Time or HERE, from this person to home, in minutes) moves the return earlier when they head home sooner than usual. A Proximity direction of travel sensor tells whether they are heading home.

fan.title: Fan
fan.description:
Your thermostat reports these fan modes: {modes}.

With fan control on, the optimizer can circulate the blower to even out rooms, but only once a room has learned what the fan does (about 4 hours of fan-only running in history) and only when it costs less than running the AC or heat harder. The fan always goes back to the normal mode when a fan window ends, when you pause the schedule, and when the integration unloads.

data.fan_control: Let the optimizer use the fan
data.fan_mode_normal: Normal mode (blower runs only with cooling)
data.fan_mode_circulate: Circulate mode (blower runs on its own)
data.fan_humidity_max: Do not circulate above this indoor humidity (%)

data_description.fan_watts: Variable speed blowers on circulate often draw 50 to 150 W; older single speed blowers 300 to 500 W.
data_description.humidity_sensor: If empty, the thermostat's own humidity reading is used when it has one. Circulating right after cooling can blow moisture off the coil back into the house.

heating.title: Heating
heating.description:
Your thermostat reports these modes: {modes}.

The heating side works like cooling: the house learns how fast your heat warms it and where the thermostat turns it on and off, and the optimizer keeps the house above these minimums at the lowest cost. In heat_cool (auto) mode the lower setpoint is the heat and the upper one the cooling, and they never come closer than the gap below.

data.min_deadband: Minimum gap between heat and cool setpoints
data.auto_mode: Switch between heat and cool for me

data_description.heat_kind: Heat pumps get cheaper warm-ups planned gently, because a big or cold-weather warm-up turns on the expensive backup strips.
data_description.min_deadband: The smallest gap your thermostat accepts between the two setpoints in heat_cool mode. ecobee defaults to 5 °F, many others to 2 or 3 °F.
data_description.auto_mode: Only for thermostats without a heat_cool mode. The integration switches to heat or cool when the forecast plan needs it, holds a mode at least 3 hours, and never overrides a mode someone set by hand that day. If Home Assistant is down the thermostat stays in its last mode.

costs.title: Energy prices and equipment
costs.description: Used to weigh heating, cooling and the fan against each other. Rough numbers are fine; savings are reported relative to your current schedule. Gas price is {gas_unit}, the furnace rating in {furnace_unit}.

data.aux_below: Backup strips run below this outdoor temperature
data.switch_below: Switch from heat pump to gas below this outdoor temperature

data_description.ac_kw: Roughly 1 kW per ton of cooling. A heat pump draws about the same while heating.
data_description.furnace_size: The input rating on the furnace label (for example 60000 BTU/h or 17.6 kW).
data_description.aux_below: Most heat pumps lock out the compressor or lean on the strips somewhere between 25 and 40 °F (-4 to 4 °C).

error.same_fan_mode: Normal and circulate have to be different fan modes.

options.dual_fuel: Dual fuel (heat pump with gas backup)

rebalance_warm.title: {room} needs more cooling air
rebalance_warm.description:
{room} ran above its comfort limit on {days} of the last 7 days (up to {worst}° over) while the rest of the house was fine, and running the fan to mix the air does not fix it. While the AC runs it sits about {gap}° warmer than the thermostat, worst around {hour}.

That points to airflow: open {room}'s supply vents or dampers a little, close them slightly in rooms that run cool, and check the return path (a closed door with no return starves a room). After adjusting, press **Vents adjusted** so the integration can measure the effect. This notice clears itself after a week without the problem.

rebalance_cold.title: {room} needs more heating air
rebalance_cold.description:
{room} ran below its comfort minimum on {days} of the last 7 days (up to {worst}° under) while the rest of the house was fine, and running the fan to mix the air does not fix it. While the heat runs it sits about {gap}° colder than the thermostat, worst around {hour}.

That points to airflow: open {room}'s supply vents or dampers a little, close them slightly in rooms that run warm, and check the return path. After adjusting, press **Vents adjusted** so the integration can measure the effect. This notice clears itself after a week without the problem.
